How to Make Beaded Hat Charms

Learn how to make the cutest beaded hat charms to add a fun and unique personal touch to any baseball cap.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:03
Instaread

Hello! Today I have a really fun craft tutorial to share with you. I’m going to show you how to make beaded hat charms. These are simple strings of fun beads that you can clip onto the brim of any baseball cap. It’s an easy craft that doesn’t take a lot of time, but it sure is fun to be able to personalize a baseball cap and and some pizazz. I love these and can’t wait to make more!

Let me walk you through every step so you can make this craft with confidence. Here’s what you’ll need:

Materials Needed

Click on any highlighted item in the supply list for more information. Affiliate links may be used.

  • Baseball Cap (any kind, but no extra work is required if it’s a mesh-back trucker style hat)
  • Embroidery Thread in a coordinating color
  • Lobster Jewelry Clasps
  • Beads
    • Colorful Clay Beads
    • Letter Beads
    • Gold Star Beads
  • Glue Stick
  • Scissors

Instructions

Step 1: The first thing we need to do is prepare the embroidery thread so that it’s easy to string through the beads. Measure across the brim of your hat, then add around 6-8 extra inches to that length and cut a piece of embroidery thread. Then rub each end of the thread across the top of a glue stick. Make sure the threads are nice and stuck together smoothly.

Let this dry for about an hour. When the glue is dry, the ends of the thread will be stiff. This makes it so that you can thread them through the beads without the different strands splitting apart. Such a great little trick!

Step 2: Now that your thread is prepared, it’s time to string your beads. I like to start with whatever I want to go in the center of the design, then work outwards on both sides to keep things symmetrical.

Step 3: You’ll know you have the right amount of beads on your thread when the beaded part is big enough to go from one end of the hat brim to the other. Tie a lobster clasp onto one end with a double knot. Then make sure all the beads are tight together and add the lobster clasp to the other end with another double knot.

Step 4: To finish it off, I like to string the thread back through three or four beads, then cut off the excess string length.

Step 5: If you have a baseball cap with a mesh back, just open the lobster clasp and hook it through the mesh to attach the charm to your hat.

If you have an all-fabric baseball cap, you’ll need to do one more step.

Step 6 (For Fabric Caps Only): Grab a length of embroidery floss or regular sewing thread that matches the color of your hat. Thread it into a sturdy needle. Poke up from the back of the hat right at the spot where you want to attach your charms. Use a small dowel, wrap the thread around the dowel, then back down into the hat. Repeat a few times to make a sturdy little loop of thread. Tie off on the underside of the hat, then slip the dowel out and you’ll have a nice little loop to attach your charm clasp to!

I think this is such a cute idea. And I love that you can make a few different ones and easily switch them out to change up the look of a hat. I made this one for the Fourth of July:

And for this one I went a bit more girly with sparkly beads and pearls:

And don’t forget that you can add dangly charms too! There are seriously just so many endless possibilities with this craft. Fun stuff!
